Platelets or thrombocytes are short-lived cell fragments that 
comprise less than 1% of the total blood volume. Unless they are
activated, they are degraded and their components are recycled 
after approximately one week. If activated by chemical media-
tors, such as the cytokines, they aggregate (cluster) to form a 
clot that is attracted to the site of an injury and is very sticky. In-
dividual clotting factors, bleeding time, clotting time, and other 
measures of platelet activity are available from laboratory panels
for standard blood samples. Th is information is useful for as-
sessing risk of clots or hereditary disorders such as hemophilia.
